indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B4.4.2.1 Demonstrate knowledge of generation of electricity, its transmission and transformation into other forms

skills.description: Recognise common appliances that use electricity (e.g. bulb, television, iron, fan, phone charger).
State simple uses of electricity: lighting, heating, cooling, entertainment, communication.
Match an appliance to its main use (e.g. iron → pressing clothes; bulb → light).
Recognise electricity as a form of energy that makes appliances work.
Give examples of electricity use at home and at school.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions total — Difficulty 1: 5; Difficulty 2: 7; Difficulty 3: 5; Difficulty 4: 3.
misconceptions: Electricity is not a form of energy.
Electricity is only used in cities.

questions.stem: Which of these uses electricity to work?
hints: Which one has a plug or needs power?
You watch pictures on it.
questions.explanation: A television uses electricity to work. Brooms, buckets and chairs do not need electricity.

questions.stem: Which of these is a use of electricity?
hints: What happens when you switch on a bulb?
Electricity can produce light.
questions.explanation: Electricity is used to make light. Other uses include heating, cooling, entertainment and communication.

questions.stem: What is an electric iron used for?
hints: It makes clothes smooth.
It uses heat.
questions.explanation: An electric iron is used for pressing clothes to make them smooth.
questions.misconception: Electric iron is used for cooking.

questions.stem: Electricity is a form of what?
hints: It makes things work.
It can be changed into light and heat.
questions.explanation: Electricity is a form of energy. It can be changed into light, heat, sound and movement.
questions.misconception: Electricity is not a form of energy.

questions.stem: Which of these uses electricity at school?
hints: What gives light in the classroom?
It has a switch.
questions.explanation: A classroom bulb uses electricity to give light. Chalkboards, desks and books do not use electricity.
questions.misconception: Electricity is only used at home.

questions.stem: Which of these appliances does NOT use electricity?
hints: Which one is made of wood and has no plug?
A wooden spoon is used for cooking.
questions.explanation: A wooden spoon does not use electricity. Fans, kettles and phone chargers need electricity.

questions.stem: Ama uses an electric fan in her room. What is the fan used for?
hints: What does a fan do to the air?
It makes you feel cool.
questions.explanation: An electric fan is used to cool the room by moving air around.

questions.stem: Which appliance is used for communication?
hints: You can call and send messages with it.
It uses electricity and has a screen.
questions.explanation: A mobile phone is used for communication. It uses electricity to work.
questions.misconception: Mobile phones do not use electricity.

questions.stem: Which of these is an example of electricity use at home?
options: Using an electric kettle to boil water
hints: Which activity needs a plug or power?
Boiling water with electricity.
questions.explanation: Using an electric kettle to boil water is an example of electricity use at home.
questions.misconception: Electricity is only used at school.

questions.stem: Why does a television stop working when there is no electricity?
options: Because it needs electricity to work
Because it does not like darkness
hints: Televisions need power.
Without electricity, appliances cannot work.
questions.explanation: A television needs electricity to work. When there is no electricity, it cannot function.
questions.misconception: A television can work without electricity.

questions.stem: Name two appliances in your home that use electricity.
hints: Think of things that need to be plugged in.
One gives light; one keeps food cold.
questions.explanation: Common appliances that use electricity include televisions, fans, bulbs, irons, kettles, fridges and phone chargers.

hints: What does a bulb do?
What does a fan do?
questions.explanation: Electricity is used for lighting, heating, cooling, entertainment, communication and many other purposes.

questions.stem: Match the appliance to its use: which pair is correct?
hints: Which appliance moves air?
A fan makes you feel cool.
questions.explanation: A fan is used for cooling the room by moving air. The other pairs are mismatched.
questions.misconception: Bulbs are used for pressing clothes.

questions.stem: Give one example of how electricity is used at school and one example of how it is used at home.
answer: at school: lights in the classroom; at home: watching television
at school: bulb; at home: iron
at school: computer; at home: fan
hints: Think of a light at school.
Think of an appliance at home.
questions.explanation: At school, electricity is used for lighting classrooms, powering computers, etc. At home, it is used for lighting, cooking, ironing, entertainment, etc.
questions.misconception: Electricity is only used in one place.

options: It is a type of food
It is a form of energy that makes appliances work
hints: What does electricity do to a bulb?
It is a form of energy.
questions.explanation: Electricity is a form of energy. It makes appliances like bulbs, fans and televisions work.
questions.misconception: Electricity is not a form of energy.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a use of electricity?
hints: Plants grow using sunlight, not electricity.
Which one is a natural process?
questions.explanation: Making a plant grow is not a use of electricity. Plants grow using sunlight and water. Electricity is used for heating, cooling and lighting.

questions.stem: A pupil lists four items: a torch, a book, a radio, a pencil. Which two items use electricity?
hints: A torch uses a battery.
A radio needs power.
questions.explanation: A torch and a radio use electricity. A book and a pencil do not.

questions.stem: A family wants to cook food faster using electricity. Which appliance should they use?
hints: Which appliance is made for cooking?
A kettle boils water, but a cooker cooks food.
questions.explanation: An electric cooker is designed for cooking food using electricity. Fans cool, irons press clothes, and kettles boil water.
questions.misconception: Any electric appliance can cook food.

questions.stem: Explain why electricity is important in our homes.
answer: it is used for lighting, cooking, cooling and entertainment
it powers appliances we use every day
it helps us do many things like lighting, cooking and ironing
hints: Think of what you use at home that needs electricity.
What would happen if there was no electricity?
questions.explanation: Electricity is important because it powers many appliances we use daily for lighting, cooking, cooling, entertainment, communication and more.
